chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: The Ubangi Club and the road manager's offer
summary: A road manager offered to manage them and they played the show and dance music at the Ubangi Club for a year.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Now, so you were saying before that you had reached this point where the fellows had said look, if you can get us some work and keep us going, we won't bother going back to school.

Oh, I happened to get a little to, at least the road manager came by the Harlem Opera House to listen that night, and he caught me backstage from the Ubangi Club which was, like the Cotton Club was in Harlem, and the Ubangi Club was there. And he told me, he said if you let me manage you, I'll put you right to work. And so, I told the fellows about it and they said we're willing to take the chance. So, they put us in the Ubangi Club. I was in there for one solid year before coming out to do anything else. And then, we went from there on. We went out to do a few one nighters and then back to the Ubangi Club. And from there, we'd go to the theaters.
Okay. So, you were in the Ubangi Club. That's around '35 or '34?
And you were there for a year.

Oh, we were playing the show and dance music. We had to do, they had a regular show like the, it's on the same style as the Cotton Club. You heard about that, where they had a lot of girls. I don't know how many. Maybe, about 10, and regular acts. So, we learned how to do a show and that's what we had to do.
